## Troubleshooting

Use these steps when sqlpipe cannot connect to Postgres or cannot write to S3.

### Postgres Connection Timeouts

Make sure that the host name and port point to the correct Postgres server.

Make sure that the database accepts traffic from your IP address.

If you use a VPN, connect to the VPN before you run sqlpipe.

If the server uses TLS, set the TLS option that your Postgres driver needs.

Run `psql` with the same host, port, user, and database.

If `psql` fails, fix the database connection before you run sqlpipe again.

### S3 Permission Errors

Make sure that the AWS identity can read the source bucket.

Make sure that the AWS identity can write to the target bucket.

If sqlpipe uses an IAM role, make sure that the session uses that role.

If the bucket uses SSE-KMS, give the identity access to the KMS key.

Run the command again after the permission change reaches AWS.
